about: Edition 4 of storm-charles.promptugal.news's decision brief on Storm Charles: the words and judgements of this edition (the lead, what to watch, the authorities' decisions, sources compared). The figures (warnings, observations, flights, notices) are drawn by tools/brief-make.mjs from the incident's data files as they stood at the as-of time. Every item is labelled fact, evidence or hypothesis and carries its source and the time read. Not a warning service: IPMA issues the warnings and ANEPC the instructions.
next: At the next big change: an IPMA message, Web Summit's word on Day 3, or the end of the storm; then an "after the storm" edition, forecast beside observations.

lead.label: fact
lead.text: IPMA has lowered its rain warnings in the South: from 12:19 to 18:00, Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria and Portalegre go from red to orange; Faro stays red (rain to 18:00, wind to 21:00). Lisbon, Setúbal and Santarém keep red rain to 18:00: red rain now covers four districts, home to about 4.04 million residents (Census 2021). Lisbon's orange wind and sea run to 21:00.

src.name: IPMA's CAP messages sent 12:18:03, MeteoAlarm feed

lead.label: fact
lead.text: Why: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16): Charles split into two centres, deepens less, and the wind will be weaker than forecast yesterday; gusts of 70 to 90 km/h in the South, up to 110 km/h exposed; persistent, at times heavy rain continues.

lead.label: hypothesis
lead.text: The backing wind puts Lisbon on the storm's north side: the centre is likely over or just south of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00, and rain is now the main hazard, near a modelled high water at about 15:10. Lisbon's strongest wind may come after the centre passes, from the north-west or west. Weaker than forecast is not an all-clear.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Rain lowered to orange in Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria and Portalegre (to 18:00); red rain stands in Lisbon, Setúbal, Santarém and Faro.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: In force: orange sea for Lisbon, Setúbal, Beja and Faro (waves 5 to 7 m, up to 13 m, to 21:00).

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Lisbon airport's forecast (TAF 11:00): at times south 20 kt gusting 35 (65 km/h) in rain; a 30% chance of thunderstorms with 40 kt gusting 55 (102 km/h).

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: CP suppresses four trains across the 25 de Abril bridge in the window it calls the most critical.

watch.label: evidence
watch.text: Madeira's schools reopen (closed in the morning by the regional civil protection).

watch.label: hypothesis
watch.text: The centre likely over or just south of Lisbon (our meteorologist, medium confidence); the ensemble's median crossing about 15:00; modelled high water about 15:10 (1.25 m above mean sea level). The test: the airport's wind turning through north to north-west means the centre has passed south.
watch.src: incident.meteorologist@ 12:24; ECMWF ensemble and tide model (incident.datascience@)

watch.label: fact
watch.text: TAF: wind turning west-north-west 12 kt by 18:00, no significant weather.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Red rain ends in Lisbon, Setúbal, Santarém and Faro; orange rain ends in Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria and Portalegre.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: TAF: at times west-north-west 17 kt gusting 27 (50 km/h).

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Lisbon's orange wind and orange sea warnings end; yellow sea (waves 4 to 5 m) to 03:00 Thursday. Faro's red wind ends.

watch.label: fact
watch.text: No IPMA warning for Lisbon above yellow on Thursday morning. IPMA's model: west wind, mean 15 to 24 km/h; showers, rain chance up to 92%.
watch.src: IPMA warnings and IPMA's hourly model (run 07:56)

watch.label: fact
watch.text: Web Summit's word on Day 3 (Thursday): it "aims to proceed as planned", an aim, not yet a decision.

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: The airport's wind: it backed from south-south-east to east-north-east in three hours while the pressure fell 4 hPa in an hour. A turn through north to north-west with rising pressure would mean the centre has passed south of Lisbon; the strongest wind may come then, from the north-west or west.

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: Thunderstorm cells (TCU or CB in the METAR): the TAF gives its strongest gusts only with thunderstorms, so a short, sharp spell is the case to watch, not a long blow.

signs.label: hypothesis
signs.text: Hourly rain above 6 mm at the city's stations around high water (about 15:10, modelled): the press reports the risk of rain and tide together hindering drainage in the big cities.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Warnings adjusted (CAP, 18 messages): rain lowered from red to orange in Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria and Portalegre, 12:19 to 18:00; Faro's red rain renewed to 18:00; no change for Lisbon, Setúbal or Santarém.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Communiqué no. 3: Charles split into two centres; wind weaker than forecast yesterday; gusts 70 to 90 km/h in the South, up to 110 km/h exposed; "the warnings were adjusted".

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Alert situation for the whole mainland, Wednesday 00:00 to 23:59: schools and non-essential public services closed; outdoor events suspended.

decided.label: fact
decided.what: Day 2 (Wednesday) will not take place, on the government's formal advice; Day 3 (Thursday) "aims to proceed as planned".

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: All of Lisbon's road tunnels closed from midnight; parks, gardens and cultural facilities too.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Four trains across the 25 de Abril bridge suppressed, 12:00 to 15:00.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Vasco da Gama bridge limited to 100 km/h because of the weather.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Service kept with priority to essential journeys; trams 12E, 15E, 18E, 24E, 25E and 28E interrupted; Graça funicular closed since 10:40; Web Summit shuttles cancelled. Fertagus trains: normal service, confirmed at 10:40.
decided.when: read 11:52 at source (no update time on the page)

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: River crossings between Lisbon and the south bank kept running from 05:00 (one crossing, Porto Brandão–Trafaria–Belém, reported suspended in the morning).

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Operations adjusted; tickets for travel to 11 Nov may be changed without penalty to flights up to 17 Nov.

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Wednesday's scheduled activity rescheduled (which hospitals: not stated).

decided.label: evidence
decided.what: Schools closed Wednesday morning, reopening from 13:00. 205 occurrences to 09:00, none classed as serious.

compare.official: Red, 09:00–18:00, no change in the 12:18 batch; communiqué no. 3: persistent, at times heavy rain continues
compare.models: TAF: rain all afternoon, heavy with a 30% thunderstorm chance 12:00–16:00
compare.obs: Heaviest hour since the red warning began: 17.9 mm Oeiras, 17.2 Relógio, 14.6 Tapada (hour 11:00); six hours to 11:00: 45.4 mm Oeiras, 41.2 Relógio
compare.press: Heavy rain about 11:00–15:00, easing after about 18:00 (radio, 10:38)
compare.assessment: What is observed matches the red rain warning in timing and character.

compare.official: 12:18 batch: red to orange in Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria, Portalegre from 12:19; Faro red to 18:00
compare.models: Communiqué no. 3: rain moving south-west to north-east
compare.obs: n/a in our data (our station table is Lisbon's)
compare.press: ECO: "eight districts in red" (the earlier count; not what the 12:18 batch says)
compare.assessment: Read the CAP messages, not the headline: four districts in red rain.

compare.official: Orange, 09:00–21:00, gusts up to 120 km/h (no change in the 12:18 batch); communiqué no. 3: wind weaker than forecast, 70–90 km/h in the South, 110 exposed
compare.models: TAF lowered twice: at times 65 km/h gusts, 30% chance of 102 km/h in thunderstorms; ECMWF ensemble gusts at Lisbon: median 69, 90th percentile 85 km/h
compare.obs: Airport east-north-east 28 km/h, no gust (12:00); highest gust since Tuesday 67 km/h (Tue 11:00)
compare.press: Reports the lowered warning; some attribute more to IPMA than it wrote
compare.assessment: IPMA's own word now meets the forecasts and the observations: a weaker wind. Lisbon's orange warning was not lowered in the 12:18 batch.

compare.official: Warnings overlap 12:00–18:00 (red rain, orange wind, orange sea)
compare.assessment: The early afternoon, to about 16:00, is the window the sources share; the peak hour within it is not known.

compare.official: Communiqué no. 3 (12:16): split into two centres north of Madeira; less deepening
compare.models: ECMWF ensemble (51 forecasts): 49% south of Lisbon, 41% near, 10% north; median crossing about 15:00
compare.obs: Wind backed south-south-east to east-north-east in three hours; pressure 994 hPa, down 4 hPa in the hour (12:00)
compare.press: Track moved south, toward the Algarve (radio, 10:38; not IPMA in writing)
compare.assessment: Over or just south of Lisbon about 13:00 to 15:00 (our meteorologist, medium confidence); north is the outlier.

compare.official: Orange sea, 12:00–21:00: waves 5–7 m, up to 13 m; yellow to 03:00
compare.models: IPMA's model: sea 3–3.5 m Thursday morning; tide model: high water about 15:10 (1.25 m), next about 03:10 Thursday
compare.obs: No gauge or buoy in our data; Instituto Hidrográfico's official table needs an account (not read)
compare.press: Rain at high tide may hinder drainage (live blog, 08:27)
compare.assessment: High water falls inside the red rain window; the warning is the written word on the sea.

compare.official: Lowered to yellow and green on IPMA's warnings page (12:24); earlier red rain to 06:00, orange wind to 12:00
compare.obs: 249.5 mm in six hours at Areeiro (01:00–06:00); airport wind dropped from 89 km/h gusts at 07:00 to 13 km/h at 08:00
compare.press: Regional president: 479 mm somewhere on the island; 205 occurrences, none serious
compare.assessment: The worst has passed Madeira; the risk now is what the rain left (slopes, streams), which only the regional civil protection can state.

compare.official: Lisbon: rain to 18:00, wind and sea to 21:00, yellow sea to 03:00; nothing above yellow on Thursday
compare.models: TAF: no significant weather from about 18:00; showers on Thursday
compare.assessment: Thursday morning looks like showers and a westerly wind, not a storm; Web Summit's Day 3 word is still awaited.

gaps.what: Precedents: Leslie (2018), Elsa (2019) and later storms, highest gust, incidents, customers without power
Tides, official: Instituto Hidrográfico's table for Lisbon, Cascais and Funchal
gaps.state: this edition uses a model (Open-Meteo Marine); IH's table needs an account and was not read

change: What changed since edition 3 (12:27): the warnings IPMA's communiqué no. 3 called "adjusted" are its CAP messages sent at 12:18:03: rain lowered from red to orange, 12:19 to 18:00, in Beja, Castelo Branco, Leiria and Portalegre; Faro's red rain renewed to 18:00; no message for Lisbon, Setúbal or Santarém, whose red rain stands. Red rain now covers four districts, not eight. IPMA's open data had not caught up when read (12:28): the grid, the map and the residents below follow the CAP messages, marked "(CAP)".
ana: 288 flights cancelled at Lisbon in advance, as reported by CNN Portugal's live page at 11:49 (222 by 09:20 at Lisbon and Faro, by the same page citing the airports' operator); not read at the operator's own site, which shows automated readers a bot check.
